analysis:
Reviewed docs/developer/build.md, a documentation-only change. Both supplied units are base-side text; the head side is visible only through the truncated patch excerpt and changed-range map. The excerpt shows a date bump, a new paragraph (head lines ~76-88) on metal-cpp handling, and CI/routing/cache wording changes in the head ranges.

Security-relevant item: the new paragraph says scripts/fetch-metallib.sh uses a local metal-cpp archive at /usr/local/libexec/darkbloom/share/metal-cpp/metal-cpp_26.zip, or one named by MLX_METAL_CPP_ARCHIVE. It accepts the archive only if its SHA-256 matches the script's pin, and then passes -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_METAL_CPP. This is a build-supply-chain input. The doc describes a hash-pinned check, so the documented control is sound if the script implements it. The script is not in this batch, so whether it actually verifies the hash before unzipping (and handles zip path traversal) is unverified. That is an integration question for the script, not a finding on this doc. The claim that the metallib and its cache key are unchanged also depends on the script.

Other changed ranges, per the range map only (patch truncated): CI job and caching descriptions and Darkbloom Sandbox routing, the build-environment table at head 509-559, App Attest lines 581-606, and verify text at 642 and 657-663. None change provider runtime code, the coordinator-to-provider contract, App Attest authorization (TB-011) or encrypted prefix-cache behavior (T-041). No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by the visible content. I could not see the full head text, so truncated CI/routing changes are unexamined; the earlier docs still state that release, signing and publication keep literal Blacksmith labels.

Recommend that the next pass check scripts/fetch-metallib.sh for hash verification, TOCTOU safety and extraction safety. No findings.
